speaker: Narrator
en: Welcome to the Practical AI Podcast, where we break down the real world applications of artificial intelligence and how it's shaping the way we live, work, and create. Our goal is to help make AI technology practical, productive, and accessible to everyone. Whether you're a developer, business leader, or just curious about the tech behind the buzz, you're in the right place. Be sure to connect with us on LinkedIn, X, or Blue Sky to stay up to date with episode drops, behind the scenes content, and AI insights. You can learn more at practicalai.fm.
zh: 欢迎来到 Practical AI 播客，在这里我们拆解人工智能的现实世界应用以及它如何塑造我们的生活、工作和创造方式。我们的目标是帮助使 AI 技术变得实用、高效且对所有人触手可及。无论你是开发者、商业领袖，还是只是对热门背后的技术感到好奇，你都来对地方了。请务必在 LinkedIn、X 或 Blue Sky 上与我们联系，以了解最新剧集发布、幕后内容和 AI 见解。您可以在 practicalai.fm 了解更多信息。

speaker: Narrator
en: Now onto the show.
zh: 现在开始今天的节目。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Welcome another episode of the Practical AI Podcast. I'm Daniel Whitenack. I am CEO at Prediction Guard, and I'm really excited today to have, an amazing guest that, I'm personally interested in asking a bunch of selfish questions too because I'm I'm so interested in the topic. But we have Emil Lassen who's the standards lead at the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company. Welcome.
zh: 欢迎收看 Practical AI 播客的另一期节目。我是 Daniel Whitenack。我是 Prediction Guard 的 CEO，今天我真的很兴奋能请到一位神奇的嘉宾，我个人也有很多自私的问题想问他，因为我太感兴趣了。但我们请到了 Emil Lassen，他是人工智能承保公司的标准负责人。欢迎。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: How how are you doing?
zh: 你你怎么样？

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Thanks, Daniel. Thanks for having me. I'm doing great. How are you?
zh: 谢谢，Daniel。谢谢你邀请我。我很好。你呢？

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: I I'm I'm doing well. Actually, you know, today in the Midwest, everyone's concerned about tornadoes and talking about hail and and some things like insurance and other things. So it's a whole other other world, of course, but, obviously, the AI underwriting company, way way more than thinking about insurance, but thinking about standards, certification around AI and agents. I'm wondering how, you personally, just to give the audience a little bit about you personally, how did you end up at this intersection of standards, certification, AI, agents? How how did that come about?
zh: 我我我很好。其实，你知道，今天在中西部，每个人都担心龙卷风，谈论冰雹，以及一些像保险之类的事情。所以这当然是另一个世界，但是，显然，人工智能承保公司，不仅仅考虑保险，而是思考关于人工智能和智能体的标准和认证。我想知道，你个人，只是为了给听众一点关于你个人的背景，你是如何最终来到标准、认证、人工智能、智能体的这个交叉路口的？这是怎么发生的？

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Yeah. So I I don't think I had as clearer path as as the classic standards lead where you work as a say, security engineer for ten years and then learn the technical craft and then come together. My journey has been very entrepreneurial always. I started my first company with actually the CEO of the artificial intelligence company, Ruininkvist, ten years ago. It was a nonprofit back then helping students from low income backgrounds get into top universities.
zh: 是的。所以我我不认为我有一条像经典标准负责人那样清晰的路径，比如作为安全工程师工作十年然后学习技术工艺然后走到一起。我的旅程一直是非常创业的。我实际上是在十年前和人工智能公司的 CEO Ruininkvist 一起创办了我的第一家公司的。那是一个非营利组织，帮助低收入背景的学生进入顶尖大学。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: And I think what I took away from that was both the very entrepreneurial journey, but also desire to move fast on some of the challenges that society is facing. I then moved in and had my first interaction with standards at my second company, a real estate company back in Denmark, where we developed an impact management system that both had to navigate a lot of national legislation, local legislation, EU legislation, voluntary frameworks, investor demands. And so had my first interaction with one of these quite complex markets of different measurements and targets you wanted to get to, a very technical sector as well where like building codes, for example, require a lot of thinking through how you do things the right way. So I spent four years building up a real estate company that today is managing about 400,000,000 together with four other co founders and took from that this desire to go in and standardize when we know what the right answer is and try to push the sector in that direction. The way I got into the AI space was taking a step back from the real estate company now a few years ago and going to Cambridge, Massachusetts, so Harvard University, where I spent two years as a fellow at the Kennedy School, really getting into the emerging tech and geopolitics of all of this as well.
zh: 我想我从那里得到的是非常创业的旅程

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: And left the Kennedy School with a very sheer ambition of just getting under the hood of the pace of AI, the safety and security aspects, and clearly just acknowledging that the technology is going to profoundly change society as we know it today. And in many different ways, I have 10 nephews and nieces, have five sisters. And seeing a 10 year old being comfortable using AI the way they are is kind of scary. And I don't see yet that we've codified the principles we want to see when it comes to how kids use AI. So that's one direction where, oh, maybe we should develop standards for this.
zh: 带着一种纯粹的抱负离开了肯尼迪学院，只想深入探究 AI 的步伐、安全与保障方面，并清楚地承认这项技术将深刻改变我们今天所知的社会。在许多不同方面，我有 10 个侄子和侄女，有 5 个姐妹。看到一个 10 岁的孩子如此自如地使用 AI，有点可怕。我还没有看到我们已经编纂了我们希望看到的原则，当涉及到孩子如何使用 AI 时。所以这是一个方向，哦，也许我们应该为此制定标准。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: You also can read news every week and see new incidents. So there's clearly a big security angle to this as well. You said that the Midwest is facing tornadoes today. I think being a CISO at a company adopting and deploying AI right now feels a little bit like you're in a hailstorm and it's only a matter of time before you're hit by some of that. We just keep seeing that.
zh: 你每周都能看到新闻，看到新的突发事件。所以这显然也有一个很大的安全角度。你说中西部今天正面临龙卷风。我认为在一家采用和部署 AI 的公司担任 CISO，感觉有点像你在遭遇冰雹风暴，被其中一些击中只是时间问题。我们一直看到这种情况。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: So clearly there was a element to that as well. And then there's the even bigger picture around what this will do to our job markets and so forth. So left the Kennedy School being very interested in just using the public policies toolbox that I brought from that with the standards toolbox I brought from my real estate company and then this desire to actually just work on societal challenges that I think has been with me since I started working. And that became my way to the artificial intelligence underwriting company. I've since then spent all my time building a network of people, a consortium, to help them figure out how we get the right practical and technical insights into the standards we develop as well.
zh: 所以显然也有这方面的因素。然后还有更大的图景，关于这将对我们的就业市场等产生什么影响。所以带着浓厚的兴趣离开了肯尼迪学院，只想使用我从那里带来的公共政策工具箱，以及我从房地产公司带来的标准工具箱，然后还有这种实际上致力于解决社会挑战的愿望，我认为这种愿望从我开始工作以来就一直伴随着我。这成为了我通往人工智能承保公司的方式。从那时起，我花了所有时间建立一个人员网络，一个财团，帮助他们弄清楚如何将正确的实践和技术见解纳入我们制定的标准中。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah. That's that's awesome. And I and I know sometimes when people hear things like standard certification, you know, terms like this, maybe some some people might have a reaction of, like, slowing things down. Right? But I I like how in at the very, you know, front and center of what you talk about is how to actually unlock enterprise adoption with, certification standards, etcetera.
zh: 是的。这很棒。我知道有时当人们听到标准认证这样的事情时，你知道，像这样的术语，也许有些人会有反应，比如，这会拖慢事情。对。但我喜欢你在谈话的最核心，你知道，谈论的是如何实际上通过认证标准等解锁企业采用。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Could you talk, before we dive into the AI side of this specifically, could you talk about that a little bit in general, like how some of these things work together in actual enterprise settings, standard certification, even insurance, and how how those things actually can enable adoption with and not just like block things, I guess.
zh: 在我们深入探讨 AI 方面的具体内容之前，你能谈谈这方面的一些一般情况吗，比如这些事情在实际企业环境中是如何协同工作的，标准认证，甚至是保险，以及这些事情实际上如何能够促进采用，而不仅仅是阻碍事情，我猜。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Happy to. So I think our story and the inspiration we take dates back to Benjamin Franklin's Philadelphia. Philadelphia was starting to adopt electricity. Electricity was scary back then. Light bulbs did not work out.
zh: 很高兴。我认为我们的故事和我们的灵感可以追溯到本杰明·富兰克林的费城。费城开始采用电力。那时电力很可怕。灯泡没有成功。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Homes started burning down. So Benjamin Franklin formed the first fire brigade in Philadelphia. He started codifying building codes so that we basically took what we knew around how to build safer houses, the standards part, and then he developed the first mutual insurance company. So back then, this is the first time we see this flywheel of standards, audits and insurance go together. By having standards around building codes, for example, you knew that houses needed to be placed a little bit further from each other.
zh: 房屋开始着火。所以本杰明·富兰克林在费城组建了第一支消防队。他开始编纂建筑规范，所以我们基本上利用了我们已知的关于如何建造更安全的房屋的知识，这是标准部分，然后他开发了第一家互助保险公司。所以在那时，这是我们第一次看到标准、审计和保险这个飞轮一起运转。通过围绕建筑规范制定标准，例如，你知道房屋需要彼此隔开一点距离。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: They needed some of his lightning rods to ensure that when lightning strikes that they catch fire. The fire inspections was the audit part that actually went in and examined that you'd followed these rules appropriately. And the insurance side mitigated the residual risk that will always be there when we introduce new powerful technology into society. We've seen this flywheel of standards audits and insurance time and time again when new technology has been introduced in society. We see it again in cars.
zh: 它们需要他的一些避雷针，以确保当闪电击中时它们会着火。消防检查是审计部分，实际上进去检查你是否适当地遵守了这些规则。保险方面缓解了将新技术引入社会时始终存在的残余风险。当新技术引入社会时，我们一次又一次地看到标准、审计和保险的飞轮。我们在汽车上再次看到了它。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Cars have safety standards. These were not demanded by government. They came from industry themselves because they knew that if we develop safer cars, people are more likely to buy them and safer cars actually enable you to drive even faster as well. So it was industry standards that also led us to airbags and seat belts and some of the other things that now make cars safer. We naturally have, again, the third party auditor going in and checking these cars and ensure that they follow the rules.
zh: 汽车有安全标准。这些不是政府要求的。它们来自行业本身，因为他们知道如果我们开发更安全的汽车，人们更有可能购买它们，而更安全的汽车实际上也能让你开得更快。所以正是行业标准也让我们有了安全气囊和安全带以及其他一些现在让汽车更安全的东西。我们自然又有第三方审计员进去检查这些汽车，并确保它们遵守规则。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: We have the inspection element again, and we also have the insurance element. And this flywheel, one of the best things about it is that it really scales. So we're not just thinking, seeing it with say light bulbs and cars. We also see it for nuclear power plants to this date where you also have standards inspections of those power plants and insurance even works in this case as well. So there's no limitation to the power of this flywheel.
zh: 我们再次有了检查元素，我们也有保险元素。这个飞轮，最好的事情之一是它真的可以扩展。所以我们不仅考虑看到灯泡和汽车有这样的情况。我们今天也看到它用于核电站，那里也有对这些电站的标准检查，保险在这种情况下也起作用。所以这个飞轮的力量没有限制。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: When we're looking at AI, we see some of the same things at play. We see a new technology that is very powerful and has the powers both do a lot of good, but also if things go wrong, can have severe financial implications. And the other thing is it's a complex industry where me as a startup saying my technology is safe creates limited trust if I'm an enterprise buyer, big bank, for example, that wants to adopt this technology. So with the artificial intelligence underwriting company, what we're trying to do is to create that trust layer in between the companies building AI and the companies adopting AI. And what we offer as the trust layer is this flywheel.
zh: 当我们看 AI 时，我们看到一些相同的事情在起作用。我们看到一种非常强大的新技术，具有做很多好事的力量，但如果出错了，也会产生严重的财务影响。另一件事是它是一个复杂的行业，我作为一家初创公司说我的技术是安全的，如果我是一个企业买家，例如一家想要采用这项技术的大银行，就会产生有限的信任。因此，通过人工智能承保公司，我们要做的是在构建 AI 的公司和采用 AI 的公司之间创建一个信任层。我们作为信任层提供的就是这个飞轮。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: So we go in and codify the standards we believe that the companies building AI should follow. We go in and audit against those standards in collaboration with third party auditors like Shellman, CoalFire, companies who really know how to go deep and validate that the standards actually followed. And then we certify companies against the standards. A big part of the certification in the case of Agenack AI is red teaming, so we go in and test the actual AI agent systems, not just to see that the policies they have are in place and work well, but that the agents actually work and are robust under pressure, and the companies that then obtain a certificate gets access to buy insurance of their agents so that there's also that financial coverage of residual risk.
zh: 所以我们进去编纂我们认为构建 AI 的公司应该遵循的标准。我们与第三方审计员（如 Shellman、CoalFire）合作，根据这些标准进行审计，这些公司真的知道如何深入验证标准实际上得到了遵守。然后我们根据标准对公司进行认证。在 Agenack AI 案例中，认证的大部分是红队测试，所以我们进去测试实际的 AI 智能体系统，不仅是为了看到他们制定的政策已经到位并且运行良好，而且是为了确保智能体真的有效并且在压力下是稳健的，然后获得证书的公司可以获得为其智能体购买保险的权限，以便也有针对残余风险的经济覆盖。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah, this is so interesting and I have so many questions. Maybe one question that's just very selfish and our listeners know some part of the joy of being able to do a podcast like this is I get to get my own questions answered by people that are smarter than me. But one of those questions that I have that actually comes up in conversations I have day to day is is this tension of, hey, I I see a standard out there, whether it's, you know, some of the standards that we'll talk about that you all are codifying, or maybe it's things like the NIST AI risk management framework or things from OWASP. And logically they say, yes, it would make sense to do those things. But what is the forcing function that is kind of making making companies consider actual implementation of those of those principles rather than having it be a be an aspirational thing?
zh: 是的，这太有趣了，我有很多问题。也许有一个问题非常自私，我们的听众知道做这样一个播客的乐趣之一是我可以回答我自己的问题，由比我更聪明的人来回答。但我有的其中一个问题，实际上在我每天的谈话中出现的，是这种紧张关系，嘿，我在那里看到了一个标准，无论是你们正在编纂的一些标准，还是像 NIST AI 风险管理框架或来自 OWASP 的东西。逻辑上他们说，是的，做这些事情是有道理的。但是强制功能是什么，促使公司考虑实际实施这些原则，而不是让它成为一种愿景性的东西？

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Is it the is it the potential, you know, PR risk to the company? Is it you mentioned the financial side, the, maybe it's the commercial side of getting, you know, software vendors getting their software into the hands of their enterprise customers. What what do you see as some of those main forcing functions, or are there even those forcing functions right now that would force people to consider this as something, you know, not aspirational but actually practical?
zh: 是对公司潜在的公关风险吗？你提到了财务方面，也许是软件供应商将他们的软件交给企业客户的商业方面。你认为那些主要的强制功能是什么，或者现在是否有那些强制功能，迫使人们将其视为某种不是愿景性的而是实际的东西？

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Yeah. So I I see a couple of different things that I think are very practical. Any vendor building powerful AI right now knows how tricky it is to get through the enterprise vendor due diligence process and questionnaires. So these startups face these questionnaires. Sometimes there's a 100 questions on them and it's extremely painful to go through.
zh: 是的。所以我看到几件我认为非常实际的事情。现在任何构建强大 AI 的供应商都知道通过企业供应商尽职调查流程和问卷是多么棘手。所以这些初创公司面临这些问卷。有时上面有 100 个问题，过程非常痛苦。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: And I can tell you also, speak to a lot of enterprise CSOs and GSE managers, it's equally painful on their side, right? Because they're at a stage where the space changes so often that they feel a desire to actually change their questionnaire every month. Going through a 100 questions from a startup every single time you try to onboard a vendor is also completely painful on the other side. So I think part one here is speed and a desire to get to a place where you actually feel like you've covered your blind spots as well. And having a third party developed standard with all of the industry in the room to help find those blind spots and figure out how we can't fight them in a standard, I think is value proposition number one.
zh: 我也可以告诉你，我也和许多企业的 CSO 和 GSE 经理谈过，这对他们来说同样痛苦，对吧？因为他们处于一个阶段，这个领域变化非常频繁，以至于他们觉得实际上每个月都有改变问卷的愿望。每次尝试入职供应商时都要回答初创公司的 100 个问题，在另一方面也是完全痛苦的。所以我认为第一部分是速度和渴望到达一个地方，在那里你实际上觉得你也覆盖了你的盲点。拥有一个由所有行业参与开发的第三方标准，在房间里帮助发现这些盲点并弄清楚我们如何在标准中对抗它们，我认为这是价值主张的第一号。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: The speed argument obviously assumes that you can get across the line in the first place. I think the second part of the value proposition is having that third party validation that your Agenack AI is actually safe, secure and reliable. We're working with some of the frontier companies in the aerospace right now, companies like Eleven Labs, companies like Fin that just got acquired for 3,600,000,000 by Salesforce, companies like UiPath who have set the standards within their categories historically. They have fantastic security postures, but they don't have a way to prove that to an enterprise. So an enterprise will just never trust a company that has an incentive to sell their product.
zh: 速度论点显然假设你首先能跨越终点线。我认为价值主张的第二部分是拥有第三方验证，证明你的 Agenack AI 实际上是安全的、有保障的和可靠的。我们正在与航空航天领域的一些前沿公司合作，比如 Eleven Labs，比如刚刚被 Salesforce 以 36 亿美元收购的 Fin，比如 UiPath，他们在历史上确立了各自类别内的标准。他们拥有 fantastic 的安全态势，但他们没有办法向企业证明这一点。所以一个企业永远不会信任一家有销售产品激励的公司。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: They need that third party to go in and do that. And then I do think there is a security argument to be made here. Our red teaming consistently uncovers blind spots for the companies that we work with. Sometimes it's the hallucination rate where we realize that a specific type of adversarial attack will bring up the hallucination rate or specific language switches or other things that might actually happen when their products are deployed. Other times, it's jailbreaking risk that we manage to uncover or pump injection risk that we manage to uncover.
zh: 他们需要第三方进去做这件事。然后我确实认为这里有一个安全论据。我们的红队测试不断为我们合作的公司发现盲点。有时是幻觉率，我们意识到某种类型的对抗性攻击会提高幻觉率，或者特定的语言转换或其他事情，可能实际上发生在他们的产品部署时。其他时候，是我们设法发现的越狱风险，或者是 pump 注入风险。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: So we do also see ourselves as helping these companies actually improve their safety, security and reliability posture, which is valuable as well. Then I'm sure there's a marketing benefit to the companies going out early and adopting a new framework and showing and demonstrating their moving in front when it comes to AI security leadership. I think that's an important branding value as well that we sometimes help provide, but I don't think that's the core benefit of decertification right now. I think that is really unlocking upmarket enterprise revenue for the for the companies.
zh: 所以我们也确实认为自己在帮助这些公司实际提高他们的安全性、保障性和可靠性态势，这也是有价值的。然后我确信公司有营销收益，早期采用新框架并展示和展示他们在 AI 安全领导力方面的前沿行动。我认为这也是一种重要的品牌价值，我们有时帮助提供，但我认为这不是目前去认证的核心利益。我认为这真的是为公司解锁高端企业收入。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Agents are impacting every function within a company, but it's sometimes very difficult to figure out what an agent should do, what a human should do. Jeffrey from News Research, a recent guest said often agents have no taste. That's why I'm so impressed with what our partner Framer is doing with their pro website builder that's already trusted by companies like Miro and Perplexity. They're implementing agents, but in a way that agents and humans work in tandem. Agents bring speed and scale, but people bring the taste, judgment, and control.

zh: 是的，不，我们非常感谢所有参与这项工作的人。我们与云安全联盟、OWASP 社区在 AIVSS 和 GinAI 项目上做了很多工作。我们与 Cisco 和 IBM 在交叉对比上合作，所以这是一个团队的努力，我真的很感激我们能够聚集生态系统围绕一个决定来透明地发布一些这些东西，以便像你们这样的组织，但我也知道大企业正在透明地使用我们发布的控制措施在他们自己的控制框架中。这是完全免费使用的，只有那些追求认证的公司实际上才需要掏钱。回到你的问题，因为我认为这是一个重要的问题，我们看待标准空间的方式是你有三层。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: You have an organizational layer, you have an infrastructure layer and then you have the agentic AI layer. At the organizational level, many organizations have been through an ISO 27,001 certification, classic management system certification. ISO then about three years ago now published the 42,001, which is the management system certification for AI systems. It's a governance certification that ensures that you have the right policies in place and the right procedures in place so that when you develop AI systems, they hopefully turn out in the right way if you follow those systems. Then you have the infrastructure layer.
zh: 你有一个组织层，你有一个基础设施层，然后你有一个智能体 AI 层。在组织层面，许多组织已经通过了 ISO 27,001 认证，典型的管理体系认证。ISO 然后大约三年前发布了 42,001，这是 AI 系统的管理体系认证。这是一个治理认证，确保你有正确的政策和适当的程序，以便当你开发 AI 系统时，如果你遵循这些系统，它们有望以正确的方式出现。然后你有基础设施层。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: That's where your SOC two comes in and your pentesting and some of the classic cybersecurity controls, access management, transport security, all the good stuff there. I'd say that many of those things become even more important in an space because pace is higher, data access is higher, so if you don't have that in order, then you should go back and ensure that you get those boxes checked. And then at the Agenack AI space, we basically just didn't see anything when we started this company and started drafting the first version of AI UC. One, we see NIST have come out with the AI risk management framework. There's a little bit of Agenack stuff in there, and I know from speaking to the team that they're considering publishing additions to this.
zh: 这就是你的 SOC 2、渗透测试和一些

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: The Cloud Security Alliance has also done their AI controls matrix, where again, there's some things in there around Agenack AI that are pretty good. The issue with both of those frameworks is that they're guidance. They're voluntary frameworks. You decide which controls you implement. You decide whether you like, how you implement them.
zh: 云安全联盟也做了他们的 AI 控制矩阵，同样，其中有一些关于 Agenack AI 的东西相当不错。这两个框架的问题在于它们是指导性的。它们是自愿框架。你决定你实施哪些控制。你决定你是否喜欢，你是如何实施它们的。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: They're not orderable frameworks. So the way AAC One fits in here is that we've basically taken the core governance things from the organizational level that we think are really important when it comes to AI systems, such as having failure plans in play when agents do not do what they're intended to do and you know how to deal with that. Good change management and acknowledging that every time you, for example, replace the LLM in an agent, it will behave differently. And if you don't take that into account in your governance, your end users will bear the burden of that. So some parts of the governance, the core parts of the infrastructure layer as well as ensuring that the folks who have access to the AI system itself and can make these big decisions, that's restricted.
zh: 它们不是可订购的框架。所以 AAC One 适应这里的方式是，我们基本上从组织层面提取了我们认为对于 AI 系统非常重要的核心治理事项，例如制定当智能体不做它们打算做的事并且你知道如何处理该情况时的失败计划。良好的变更管理并承认每次你例如替换智能体中的 LLM 时，它的行为都会不同。如果你不在你的治理中考虑到这一点，你的最终用户将承担其后果。所以治理的某些部分，基础设施层的核心部分以及确保那些可以访问 AI 系统本身并可以做出这些重大决策的人员受到限制。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: Ensuring again that transport security, when you do agent to agent communications and so forth, is in place. But otherwise, we basically leave ISO and TUC2 to do what they're really good at and focus on the agentic layer. And what is up there then for us is specific controls around safety, for example, ensuring that agents behave according to brand and that they don't give users guidance on medical care or legal advice, financial advice, other high risk areas, basically that they stay within their scope and don't start breaking out of that. We look at specifically how you restrict the agent's data access, its system access and its tool access, so it doesn't start processing refunds when you shouldn't. We look at hallucinations, which is also a risk that is quite unique to AI obviously and does not come up in any way in either ISO or SOC certifications.
zh: 再次确保传输安全，当你做智能体到智能体的通信等等时，已经到位。但除此之外，我们基本上让 ISO 和 TUC2 去做他们真正擅长的事情，并专注于智能体层。那上面对于我们来说是在安全方面的特定控制，例如，确保智能体的行为符合品牌，并且它们不给用户提供医疗护理或法律建议、金融建议、其他高风险领域的指导，基本上就是它们保持在范围内，并且不开始突破那个范围。我们具体看你如何限制智能体的数据访问，它的系统访问和它的工具访问，所以它不会在你不应该的时候开始处理退款。我们看幻觉问题，这显然也是 AI 独有的一种风险，并且不会以任何方式出现在 ISO 或 SOC 认证中。

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: So really focus on the agentic layer there and the core part of the differentiation, I'd say, is then the technical level of the controls. We go in and are actually quite prescriptive in what we want to see from the agents because we have a good understanding now of what the right toolbox is to ensure that these agents behave safe, secure and reliably. And the other thing is we acknowledge that a technical control in itself might not hold up under robustness. So six of the 40 mandatory requirements in AAC one have to do with red teaming, testing that these technical controls then hold up under pressure, both when we react, like we engage with the system as a benign user, just ask it questions and see if it hallucinates, but also what happens when we start approaching the system like, with social engineering and and adversarial pressure.
zh: 所以真的专注于那里的智能体层，并且差异化的核心部分，我会说，是控制的技术层面。我们进入并且实际上对我们要从智能体那里看到的东西相当规定化，因为我们要现在很好地理解了什么是正确的工具箱来确保这些智能体安全、可靠地行为。另一件事是我们承认技术控制本身可能在鲁棒性下站不住脚。所以 AAC one 中 40 个强制性要求中有 6 个与红队测试有关，测试这些技术控制随后在压力下站得住脚，既包括当我们反应时，像我们作为良性用户与系统互动，只是问它问题并看它是否产生幻觉，也包括当我们开始接近系统时会发生什么，像用社会工程学和对抗性压力。

speaker: Emil Lassen

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: I could very well see that new frameworks, so an AIAC two, AIAC three come out in the future. speaker: Emil Lassen

speaker: Emil Lassen

speaker: Emil Lassen
en: If you have a generative AI product, you need to define who owns the inputs and outputs and how you retain user data and whether you train on that user data.
